research.use: Application-owned function execution, matching call/output IDs, automatic continuation and explicit strict false for optional Chat-style parameters.
Distinguish Codex thread/turn approvals from the active Responses relay; no app-server approval responder or application permission modification was added.

limitations: No real provider sign-in, quota spend or function/image/Sites generation was performed. Synthetic provider acceptance and empty-pool local checks do not establish real account capability.

Callbacks execute in the application consuming the SDK, never on the relay host. Registration authorizes only those callbacks; owner checks and any external application approval requirements remain the caller responsibility.

Only GALX automatic function execution and model continuation were changed. The active Responses transport does not use Codex app-server approval requests; Codex application, managed sandbox and global approval settings were not changed.
The default remains ten model steps, including final synthesis. Positive maxSteps and AbortSignal control duration; no unlimited loop or automatic retry of uncertain work is provided.

Duplicate call IDs are blocked within a run and supplied history. New IDs are new actions; callback side effects need domain idempotency. Restarting an SDK process has no durable exactly-once callback guarantee.
Executable safeParse schemas validate locally when supplied. Plain JSON schemas constrain the provider request but do not themselves implement local callback validation.
Both relays accept client-owned functions as text inference. Standard still rejects Sites, images and provider-hosted tools; cross-pool discovery, fallback and credentials remain prohibited.

Both runtime images were replaced locally with execution closed, preserving named state volumes and central ownership waits. Central and monitor images, database schema, assignments, quotas and activation flags were unchanged.
The workspace SDK source is updated; no external SDK package was published and no public application or cloud runtime was deployed.
The compiled scan covered 669 browser/rendered assets and named private markers. It is not live authenticated UI acceptance or a claim that every public configuration identifier is absent.
